items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: and then from the Jimmie Noone band, I went to New York to play for Benny Carter.

ctx.x: That's when I first heard live, Jimmie Noone, when Zinky was the piano player. So it was a privilege

for me to work with Jimmie Noone, and that'd be the last band I worked with in Chicago, and then from the Jimmie Noone band, I went to New York to play for Benny Carter. Benny Carter came out to Chicago.

I remember that -- I remember that very well, that's where I came in, because you were out there and I had yet to meet you and Keg Johnson, who was my dear friend, one of the dearest friends I ever had in life, and I remember the fact that you were in New York to join Benny Carter, and it was the talk of Chicago -- Teddy Wilson is going to New York! You know, all the local musicians were saying, man, he finally made it!

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Can we talk now about the very important personnel change you made by getting Teddy Wilson and how that particular discovery came about?

ctx.x: Can we talk now about the very important personnel change you made by getting Teddy Wilson and how that particular discovery came about?
Well, I think—not I think; I know—we were playing. I was with Fletcher Henderson, and we were playing somewhere in maybe . . . gee, what’s the big town in Rhode Island, Providence?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: And I talked to Teddy, and he finally consented to come to New York

ctx.x: So, how did Teddy Wilson join -- it was this group that Teddy Wilson joined when he came to New York?

Yes, that was about 1933, when I had been playing with Fletcher sometime before then, we were playing a date in Providence, Rhode Island, and following that engagement that night, we had a night off. Roy Eldridge suggested we drive up to hear Speed Webb and Speed Webb had a very fine pianist that Roy thought I would like.
